s-H0yY1OPII.title: The UNTHINKABLE is About to Happen to Stocks (Emergency Update)
s-H0yY1OPII.creator: Tom Nash
s-H0yY1OPII.summary: Tom Nash's emergency update, published 8 November 2026, responds to the S&P 500 falling 3% in five days and 5% in thirty days, with Friday the worst day since COVID for stocks - chip stocks down 12% and the Nasdaq down 6% - after an AI-led sell-off. His core argument is that the panic is normal sentiment, not deteriorating fundamentals: 5% drops have happened 25 times in 15 years, and the S&P is up 500% over that period. He walks through Microsoft (up 1,800% in 15 years despite two 30% drops), Nvidia (up 500% in five years despite a 54% drop in 2022) and Palantir (up 1,600% since IPO despite three 40%+ drops), arguing every drop was a buying opportunity because earnings kept improving. He distinguishes sentimental crashes, where profits keep growing and recovery takes weeks or months, from fundamental crashes like 2008, which took five years - and with S&P profits growing 30% and a 33% full-year guide, he puts this in the first bucket. He dismisses data-center ban fears at federal level (no votes to beat a filibuster or override a veto) and in Texas (a pause already passed in September; 2026-28 projects proceed). He sold zero shares and changed nothing: his system buys 10-20% below 52-week highs using cash freed by trimming at +50%, +100% and +150% gains. The video closes with a pitch for his academy (41,000 students). Garbled caption spot: the ban legislation is rendered 'BTTF 4 / Back to the Future 4'.

XHNZMOhHa8g.title: I Just Bought $74,000 in this Crushed AI Stock
XHNZMOhHa8g.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
XHNZMOhHa8g.summary: Joseph Hogue's weekly market update, published 8 November 2026, is a dip-buying tour of 29 AI stocks after a brutal sell-off: the Nasdaq is down over 10% from its peak into correction territory, Nvidia is down 22% in a month and Micron 34%, with Marvell down 50%. He argues the sell-off is overdone because nothing fundamental has changed - hyperscalers plus Oracle are set to spend over $1 trillion on AI in 2027, already locked in and funded - and because a data-center construction slowdown was coming anyway for physical reasons (power generation takes years, high-bandwidth memory is short), so the post-midterm political fears change the messaging, not the demand. He screens five groups - AI infrastructure, memory, AI power, cybersecurity and software - on forward revenue growth and PEG ratio, finding a wide gap between collapsing prices and still-strong fundamentals, AMD being the clearest example (revenue +45%, data-center revenue +97%, yet down a third). His headline action is a real purchase: 700 shares of ServiceNow at $106 each, $74,000, on its orchestration story. He would also pick up Palantir, Micron, SanDisk, Bloom Energy, Fortinet and Zscaler, while holding Palo Alto, CrowdStrike, Okta and Cloudflare as too expensive to add, and pulling back on Arista after its earnings pop. A sponsored Gigastar segment interrupts the analysis. ddW_RCLYdJ4.title: 5 Stocks to Buy in the Biggest Market Opportunity Nobody Sees
ddW_RCLYdJ4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
ddW_RCLYdJ4.summary: Published 5 November 2026, this video argues the next big energy opportunity is hiding in plain sight: oilfield equipment and services. Hogue recaps his August call on the explorers - ConocoPhillips up 71%, Devon up 60%, Diamondback up 56% over the last year, with energy the top sector at +53% and profits up 108% - but notes the equipment and services names were left behind (Halliburton +34%, Baker Hughes +14%, Liberty Energy just +3%) because the majors capped spending to protect prices and return cash instead. His core argument is that this discipline cannot last: nearly 90% of upstream investment since 2019 has only offset declining production, and without continued investment global output would fall about 8% a year, from 100 million barrels a day toward 20 million by 2040, while Goldman Sachs sees demand rising to 110 million by 2035. On top of that forced reinvestment he stacks three catalysts - a $183 billion Venezuela restoration, a $58 billion Middle East rebuild, and AI data centers needing some $3 trillion of infrastructure by 2030. His five picks are SLB, Halliburton, Baker Hughes, Kodiak Gas Services and Liberty Energy, with Kodiak the most emphatic buy and Liberty the one to pass on at 99 times earnings; among the explorers he still favours Diamondback and Devon on valuation. Note: the captions garble some figures (ConocoPhillips is quoted up 71% early on and 75% later; Liberty is +3% in one passage and down 8.5% in another; Kodiak's expected revenue growth figure is missing/garbled), and 'shell explorer' is shale, 'Exo-XOMs' is Exxon.

XpvoTf97TsE.title: Jensen Huang Affair and Nvidia Board Probe: What It Means for NVDA
XpvoTf97TsE.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
XpvoTf97TsE.summary: Jose Najarro's 9 November 2026 episode covers Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of infidelity - a message to the company on Sunday 8 November saying 'I was unfaithful to my wife' - and the board's independent investigation. The woman is reported by major outlets as a former executive at Mega Speed, a private Singapore-based GPU cloud company and Nvidia customer under scrutiny since October 2025 over whether banned Nvidia chips reached China. Najarro stresses three separate buckets: one confirmed admission, one company under scrutiny, and serious but anonymously sourced allegations - the New York Times reported US intelligence concluded the executive collected information for Beijing and was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, with a classified memo said to have been overseen by Secretary Rubio. The Chinese embassy called the allegations unfounded; Singapore said there was no investigation of her alleged intelligence ties, though its police probe into Mega Speed continues. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, and Jensen stays CEO without interruption. His take: Nvidia is bigger than one person and the business is intact - hyperscalers keep buying, no cancellations expected - but Jensen's word now carries less weight with him personally. ncslbnvnaMI.title: Nvidia Stock Down 22% — Is Its 13x Forward P/E a STEAL?
ncslbnvnaMI.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
ncslbnvnaMI.summary: Jose Najarro's 8 November 2026 episode argues Nvidia, down 22% from its early-October high of around $240 to roughly $186, is a steal at a 13.1x forward P/E - the cheapest of the group he compares, against Broadcom at 15.4x, TSMC at 17.3x, Google and Meta in the 18s, Amazon at 23x, Microsoft at about 25x and AMD at roughly 32x. His thesis rests on capital expenditure: Microsoft ~$170B, Alphabet ~$200B, Amazon ~$220B and Meta ~$140B, with spending rising in calendar 2027 and, he predicts, 2028 too. The market, he says, is not worried about the next 12 months but about the cycle ending in 24-36 months; he does not believe it ends in 24 months, and even Oracle's investor-day suggestion that capex peaks around 2028 would only lift Nvidia from ~13x to ~15x if the step-down is flat or -5%. Nvidia is not just a chip, he argues, but full-stack AI factories - GPUs, CPUs, NVLink, Spectrum-X and CUDA - with Blackwell worth ~$25B per gigawatt and Vera Rubin ~$40B. AMD's data-center growth of 97% year over year is a positive read-through, since supply - not demand - is the constraint, though competition from Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium, AMD and custom ASICs is real. At ~$187, a 15x multiple implies $213, and even a 20% earnings cut leaves the stock fairly valued. Garbled caption spots: 'Nebas' for Nebius, 'IN'/'Iran' for IREN, 'Grockbot' for Grok, 'Envy Link' for NVLink, 'Capix' for capex.

JozmYeJl-XM.title: Hims & Hers Collapses 30% In a Week
JozmYeJl-XM.creator: Asymmetric Investing
JozmYeJl-XM.summary: Travis Holien (Asymmetric Investing) reacts to Hims & Hers' Q3 2026 earnings, published 10 November 2026, after the stock fell about 18% in late trading and roughly 40% over the past month — the title's '30% in a week' figure is not repeated in the captions. Revenue rose 49% year over year, but he argues the headline flatters the quarter because much of the growth came from the Eucalyptus acquisition, and management guided Q4 revenue slightly down. The core problem is mix: gross margin fell from about 83% to 57% as sales shifted to branded GLP-1s, though gross profit dollars still rose. Subscribers fell by about 100,000 quarter over quarter as the company moved away from low-cost ED and hair-loss products toward $150-plus monthly GLP-1s, TRT and peptides, while monthly revenue per subscriber climbed. SG&A fell nearly $20 million as marketing was pulled back ahead of 2027 launches, and full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut. He flags two red flags: no 2030 guidance and no earnings presentation this quarter. The positives are TRT, peptides launching later in November (Sermorelin, glutathione, NAD+ first, BPC-157 and TB-500 later) made in-house in the US, and Andrew Huberman joining the board as an adviser. His call is a HOLD: he is not selling his shares and still sees a great company over 5–10 years on a subscription-health, Costco-style model, but he is no longer in buying mode and says management must prove the strategy over the next few quarters. Zeta Global gets only a passing mention as the new No. 2 holding; no call.

fpJfxrgZz1o.title: Buy The Dip On Nvidia Or Wait It Out?
fpJfxrgZz1o.creator: Daniel Pronk
fpJfxrgZz1o.summary: Daniel Pronk answers viewer requests on Nvidia after a 27% correction left it at a 15x forward P/E, the lowest since 2012. The sell-off follows CEO Jensen Huang admitting an affair with Alice Wang, who US officials allege was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and whose network allegedly moved $7.5bn of Nvidia chips to China; the board has opened an independent investigation and the Justice Department is investigating Mega Speed, not Nvidia or Jensen. Pronk reads Jensen's apology note to staff and rejects speculation about an open relationship. He compares past CEO-affair cases (HP, Best Buy, Booking, Intel, TI, Amazon, Microsoft, Google): stocks fell on the news but the businesses mostly kept growing, so affairs alone did not decide long-term prices. His worry is specific to Nvidia: Jensen is the face of AI, there is no succession plan, and 60 directors report directly to him, so losing him would be disruptive. His DCF on analyst estimates (15% earnings growth to 2034, 25x terminal P/E) implies ~18% annual returns over 8 years, and if margins hold today's prices look cheap — but he is not a buyer, citing margin risk from Google, Amazon and AMD competition and an eventual AI capex slowdown, and says he finds better certainty in Amazon, Meta and an electrical-infrastructure holding. KB6BUs0VDrE.title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
KB6BUs0VDrE.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
KB6BUs0VDrE.summary: Joseph Hogue ranks 60 AI stocks by growth-adjusted price-to-sales and free cash flow to find the nine cheapest after a month-long AI sell-off that took the Nasdaq into correction, worsened by midterm election fears over data-centre opposition. He also re-ranks by price-to-free-cash-flow, flagging Adobe and Salesforce as cheap but facing AI demand destruction, and Micron as cheap despite memory cyclicality. MEcTLSQUA1s.title: 11 Stock Portfolio that Beats the Market
MEcTLSQUA1s.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
MEcTLSQUA1s.summary: Joseph Hogue builds an 11-stock dividend portfolio, one pick from each S&P 500 sector, arguing income beats inflation better than waiting for prices to fall. Rowe Price (TROW, financials, 4.9% yield, 40 straight annual increases), UPS (industrials, 6% yield, but his least favourite — payout ~120% of earnings, and he would swap it out), Vici Properties (VICI, real estate, 7.4% yield, his favourite, holding for a rebound), Ford (F, discretionary, 4.8% yield, cheap but a weak dividend history), Edison International (EIX, utilities, 5.9% yield, 22 straight increases, wildfire risk) and Verizon (VZ, communication services, 6.3% yield, $25bn buyback). FSPJxUCsswI.title: Why NVIDIA Is in Trouble: 7 Reasons to Sell After the Scandal
FSPJxUCsswI.creator: Asymmetric Investing
FSPJxUCsswI.summary: Travis Hoyt argues Nvidia is in trouble after Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November (CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO) and lays out seven reasons not to buy the dip. First, Nvidia was built around Huang — 60+ direct reports, reading 100 emails a day, the driving force behind CUDA — and no successor, least of all the CFO, can replace that vision. Second, China demand will dry up as the US cracks down on chips reaching China, pressuring revenue and the 75% gross margin. Third, the neocloud circular financing Huang created (funding customers like CoreWeave, who then buy Nvidia chips) falls apart without him; CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN all fell on the news. Fourth, hyperscalers (Alphabet's TPUs, Amazon's Trainium) gain leverage and will push for better pricing. Fifth, startup funding shrinks as one of the ecosystem's biggest funders exits, while hyperscalers are collectively free-cash-flow negative. Sixth, a brain drain is likely as rivals poach Nvidia talent. Seventh, the Nvidia premium — operational and valuation — is gone; even at low-teens forward earnings the stock could grind lower for three to five years. He holds no Nvidia in his portfolio. (Auto-captions garble some names, e.g. 'Jensen Wong' for Huang.)

h4k6-xHcwlw.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Is OUT — Why I'm NOT Selling NVDA Stock!!
h4k6-xHcwlw.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
h4k6-xHcwlw.summary: Jose Najarro, recording on vacation, says he is not selling any Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigned and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. His core argument is that Huang, famously paranoid about key-man risk, built a management architecture where everyone knew everything, so the company can survive without him; the hard decisions (annual chip cadence, neocloud investments, DGX Cloud, supply-chain build-out) are already made and the AI wave still has years of runway, so the new CEO mostly has to follow the existing road map. At roughly 10-11x forward earnings he calls the stock extremely cheap with the risk priced in, and he does not expect it to go south over the next two to three years. The real risks are uncertainty: possible legal liability if the affairs involved abuse of power or the alleged Chinese spy, Jensen starting a rival company or poaching talent if he is angry about being pushed out, and whether the permanent CEO (he prefers an internal candidate) has the vision for what comes after AI. He also notes CoreWeave reported much better earnings than Nebius, says he has been actively buying CoreWeave in the $44-48 range and is still bullish on Nebius. (Auto-captions garble some names, e.g. 'Cororeef' for CoreWeave.)

Mw5EXAyrPr4.title: Here Are The Top 2 Stocks I'm Buying Now
Mw5EXAyrPr4.creator: Daniel Pronk
Mw5EXAyrPr4.summary: Daniel Pronk gives an update on the two stocks he has been buying most aggressively over the past week: Nu Holdings (NU, called 'New Bank' throughout the captions) and Construction Partners (ROAD). On Nu, he walks through Q3 earnings reported the day before: revenue up 37% year over year to $6.3 billion, gross profit up 35%, earnings up 31%, return on equity of 32%, credit portfolio up 33%, and 3.7 million new customers taking the total to 143 million, serving 65% of Brazil's adult population. Mexico is now at 16.6 million customers (up 27%) after winning a banking charter, Colombia at 6.1 million (up 62%), and the US launch is under way. The one blemish is 90-day non-performing loans ticking up to a three-year high, but a 234% coverage ratio leaves him unworried. At about 14x trailing and 11.8x forward earnings he calls it still undervalued; his DCF gives a 26.4% annual return over three years on conservative assumptions (20% earnings growth, 17x terminal multiple) and 39% on more realistic ones. On Construction Partners, he summarises a 30-minute CEO conference appearance: the CEO owned the Q4 guide miss (diesel prices up 40%, bad weather), guided FY27 to 15% revenue and EBITDA growth (7% organic, 8% acquisitions) with $290 million of acquired revenue already banked, which Pronk reads as sandbagging, and reaffirmed the 2030 targets of $6 billion revenue and $1 billion EBITDA. At about 8.3x trailing EBITDA, the cheapest since the 2020 crash, his DCF gives a 22.7% annual return to 2030. He notes Nu and MercadoLibre carry similar risks, so Nu is not a huge position, but he remains bullish on both and keeps adding.

WmjFbYz-RYA.title: BUY HEAVY! These 5 Stocks Will Make Millionaires
WmjFbYz-RYA.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
WmjFbYz-RYA.summary: Joseph Hogue, a former Marine, argues drone warfare is a fundamental, decades-long shift, not a temporary war-driven surge: cheap FPV drones now account for about 60% of Russian losses in Ukraine, while the Iran conflict showed defending against them is expensive, creating a new counter-drone market. The five pure-play drone stocks soared after 2022 (Red Cat and AeroVironment up over 600% by January) then crashed roughly 58-67% from their peaks on defence-budget uncertainty, stretched valuations (90-120x earnings at the peak) and contract execution risk, including a cancelled $1.7 billion Space Force deal at AeroVironment. He compares all five on growth, profitability and valuation: AeroVironment (AVAV), the established leader with combat-proven Switchblade munitions and BlueHalo counter-drone/directed-energy tech, 45% forward revenue growth, about 11% EBITDA margin, 3.1x sales, average analyst target $210 (+68%); Kratos (KTOS), jet-powered XQ-58 Valkyrie drones, 24% growth, 5.5% margin, 4x sales, target $75 (+103%); Red Cat (RCAT), Black Widow Army recon pick plus FPV and a Palantir partnership, 128% growth, 7x sales, target $13.25 (+197%); Ondas (ONDS), the broadest platform with $757 million backlog and an $11 billion-plus pipeline, 420% growth but deeply negative margins, 12.6x sales, target about $19 (+227%); and Dragonfly (DPRO), the smallest and riskiest at about $118 million market cap, 77% growth, 15x sales, target $10 (+227%). His picks are AVAV and RCAT, with KTOS a maybe; he is holding off on DPRO.
